descriptions.loss: The loss training minimizes, averaged over the epoch's training steps. With the default loss function, policy_loss + value_loss.
descriptions.policy_loss: Cross-entropy of the network's policy against the search's policy target (its visit counts, or Gumbel MuZero's completed-Q policy), averaged over the epoch's training steps.
descriptions.value_loss: Half the squared error of the network's value against its target (the game's outcome for the player to move, mixed with the search's value with value_target_q), averaged over the epoch's training steps.
descriptions.policy_target_entropy: Entropy of the search's policy targets (nats), averaged over the epoch's training steps: the part of policy_loss no network can lower. It changes with the search and the target (more sims, a kept tree, completed-Q), so compare policy_kl, not policy_loss, across runs that differ in those.
descriptions.policy_kl: policy_loss - policy_target_entropy: the KL divergence from the search's policy targets to the network's policy (nats), averaged over the epoch's training steps. How well the network fits its targets, whatever they are.
descriptions.learning_rate: The learning rate, averaged over the epoch's training steps. Logged when the optimizer schedules it.
descriptions.weight_decay: The weight decay, averaged over the epoch's training steps. Logged when the optimizer schedules it.
descriptions.weight_norm: ||w||: the norm of the weights weight decay applies to (not biases or BatchNorm scales and offsets).
descriptions.update_ratio: ||update|| / ||w||: an optimizer step's size relative to the weights it moves, over the weights weight decay applies to. Under BatchNorm this, not the learning rate, says how fast a convolution moves; with AdamW it settles near sqrt(2 * learning rate * weight decay).
descriptions.tree_batch_fraction: The fraction of each training batch that is search tree positions rather than played positions.
descriptions.tree_buffer_samples: Search tree positions in the replay buffer that training can sample.
descriptions.moves: Self-play moves played this epoch, in all environments.
descriptions.episodes: Self-play games that ended this epoch.
descriptions.buffer_samples: Experiences in the replay buffer that training can sample, data transforms' copies included.
descriptions.buffer_distinct_positions: Distinct observations among the replay buffer's experiences.
descriptions.buffer_distinct_fraction: buffer_distinct_positions / buffer_samples. A fall means self-play is collapsing into the same few games.
descriptions.episode_draw: The fraction of the self-play games that ended this epoch that were drawn.
descriptions.episode_*: An episode_metrics_fn metric, averaged over the self-play games that ended this epoch.
descriptions.tree_positions: Search tree positions stored this epoch, besides the positions played (not counting data transforms' copies).
descriptions.tree_positions_per_move: Search tree positions stored per self-play move.
descriptions.tree_mean_visits: The mean visits of the search tree positions stored this epoch.
descriptions.search_iterations: MCTS iterations a self-play search runs, per move.
descriptions.cycles_per_move: Search cycles (the root's evaluation and each iteration) per self-play move played, counting cycles spent waiting for a move to be played: self-play's compute per move.
descriptions.*_level*_sims*_game: A game the network, searching sims iterations a move, played against the engine at that level, with its opening.
descriptions.*_game: A test game of the tester it's named after, with what each move's search explored.
descriptions.*_level*_sims*: The network's score against the engine at that level, searching sims iterations a move (a win 1, a draw 0.5, a loss 0), from watch.py.
descriptions.*_avg_outcome: The network's mean outcome in test games (a win 1, a draw 0, a loss -1) against the opponent it's named after; for a TwoPlayerTester, against the best network so far.
descriptions.*_rung: Ladder rungs beaten so far: the next test plays the rung above.
descriptions.*_score: The ladder's score against this rung's opponent (a win 1, a draw 0.5, a loss 0). Past promote_score, the ladder moves up.
descriptions.*_win_rate: The fraction of the test games against this opponent the network won.
descriptions.*_loss_rate: The fraction of the test games against this opponent the network lost.
descriptions.*_seconds: Seconds the ladder's games against this rung took, compiling included the first time it's played.
descriptions.*_top1*: How often the network's most likely action is one of the engine's best, on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a game phase: opening, midgame or endgame). No search.
descriptions.*_exp_regret*: The score the network's policy gives up against the engine's best action, expected over its policy, on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). Less noisy than regret, but it also measures how sharp the policy is: compare it only between runs with the same search and policy target (across them, use regret and value_mse). No search.
descriptions.*_regret*: The score the network's most likely action gives up against the engine's best, on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). No search.
descriptions.*_value_mse*: (value - z)^2 of the network's value, z the outcome the engine predicts (+1, 0 or -1), on the engine-labelled positions (a suffix names a group). No search.
descriptions.*_value_sign*: How often the network's value has the sign of the outcome the engine predicts, over the engine-labelled positions it doesn't call a draw (a suffix names a group). No search.
